method: Post-readback predator-fixed, guild+prey-stage and footprint matched nondocumented alternative prey; GBIF 1° stage-grid month phase ratio

matched_pairs_each_threshold.bootstrap_qualification: conditional on original matched GBIF source and prey control lists, not uncertainty in metaweb truth
conditional on original matched GBIF source and prey control lists, not uncertainty in metaweb truth

boundaries: These prey controls are UNDOCUMENTED in the available 881 complete-stage GloBI set, not demonstrated ecological non-prey.
Matching used prey-stage report volume and shared grid-year footprint before checking month synchrony.
A 1° cell across one month is not a pond, live attack, species encounter or local food web.
Repeated prey, predator, iNaturalist source and metaweb rows are not independent; phase ratios are observational and highly effort-biased.
Control species and focal interactions were defined using the same curated GloBI/GBIF ecosystem and might reflect unequal reporting.
Plant cover and rain effects are unmeasured here; do not infer causality or true stage-specific reversal.
Small focal set, no global prevalence, no p-value, and comparisons after viewing phase-shift data are exploratory.
study: Post-readback application of same guild-stage prey control to expanded 2026-09 GloBI×2026-08 GBIF Anura/Odonata global stage links
scientific_bounds: No actual predator-prey attack, abundance, wetland vegetation, rainfall or frog chorus was measured.
Same-guild/stage matched alternatives are undocumented in full-stage GloBI subset, not non-interactors.
The expanded sample is dominantly adult Anura/Odonata and thus does not validate worldwide larval role reversal.
GBIF source is anonymous 2026-08 experimental partitions, not official DOI-traceable October bulk download.
GBIF stage reporting within 1° month-year is highly seasonally and spatially biased.
If controls are too rare or 8 distinct predator taxa are unavailable, inferential uncertainty is not estimated.
